attributes.law_candidate: when a target keeps two textually-adjacent, semantically-identical pointer expressions (same base+offset, e.g. `cam` used in an early loop and `c0` used after) in DISTINCT saved registers instead of coalescing them, hoisting the SECOND expression's initializer earlier so its live range OVERLAPS the first's can force MWCC's allocator to also keep them distinct -- but the hoist point matters a lot (too early disturbs unrelated prologue scheduling and can regress; right at natural entry, before intervening calls, worked best here). Companion to claim.law.whole-fn-address-cache; this is about preventing coalescing rather than creating a cache.
